result.summary: The intersection is equipped with basic pedestrian infrastructure including marked zebra crosswalks, pedestrian signals, and curb ramps. However, the presence of embedded trolley tracks and the lack of physical traffic calming or refuge islands increases the risk for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Embedded Trolley Tracks
hazards.description: Metal tracks in the roadway can be slippery when wet and present a trip hazard for pedestrians or a wheel-catch hazard for cyclists.
hazards.location_in_image: Running down the center of the main roadway through the intersection

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles near the corner can block the view between pedestrians and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the street near the intersection

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to reduce the crossing distance and improve visibility by moving pedestrians further into the street before they cross.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking near the intersection to ensure clear sightlines for both drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signals to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before the parallel vehicle traffic gets a green light.

result.summary: The intersection features zebra-marked crosswalks and traffic signals, but lacks dedicated pedestrian signal heads and modern accessibility features. The pavement and sidewalks are in fair condition with visible wear and cracking.

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian signals
hazards.description: Pedestrians must rely on vehicular traffic lights, which can lead to confusion or unsafe crossings.

hazards.name: Degraded pavement and sidewalks
hazards.description: Visible cracking and uneven surfaces on both the roadway and sidewalks present tripping hazards.
hazards.location_in_image: Throughout the foreground and intersection area

interventions.title: Pedestrian Signal Installation
interventions.description: Add dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear right-of-way information.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk at the corners to reduce crossing distance and improve pedestrian visibility.

interventions.title: ADA Accessibility Upgrades
interventions.description: Reconstruct curb ramps to include detectable warning surfaces and ensure proper slopes.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a marked crosswalk and a sidewalk, but safety is compromised by streetcar tracks embedded in the roadway and faded pavement markings. A significant portion of the image is obscured by a blur, and trash bags obstruct the curb area near the crossing.

hazards.name: Streetcar tracks in crosswalk
hazards.description: The metal tracks embedded in the roadway create a tripping hazard and can be slippery for pedestrians, especially in wet conditions.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground, running through the crosswalk

hazards.name: Sidewalk obstruction
hazards.description: Large piles of trash bags are placed on the sidewalk and curb area, narrowing the navigable path for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image, near the utility pole

hazards.name: Faded crosswalk markings
hazards.description: The zebra-style crosswalk markings are significantly worn and faded, reducing their visibility to approaching drivers.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Markings
interventions.description: Repaint the crosswalk with high-visibility thermoplastic markings to improve driver awareness of the crossing.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear information on when it is safe to cross.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions to shorten the crossing distance and improve sightlines between pedestrians and drivers.

result.summary: The intersection features a marked zebra crosswalk and signalized control, providing a basic level of pedestrian protection. However, the crossing distance remains relatively wide without physical narrowing, and mature trees on the corner may partially obstruct sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Mature trees on the left corner may block sightlines between approaching drivers and pedestrians waiting to enter the crosswalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Left foreground corner near the traffic signal pole

hazards.name: Unprotected Crossing Exposure
hazards.description: The lack of curb extensions or a median refuge increases the time pedestrians are exposed to vehicle traffic while crossing.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the center of the roadway

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk at the corners to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Adjust signal timing to provide pedestrians with a 3-7 second head start before the parallel vehicle traffic receives a green light.

interventions.title: Vegetation Management
interventions.description: Prune or manage the trees on the corner to ensure clear sightlines for all road users at the intersection.
